Each PDF is selectable text, not an OCR reconstruction. Word counts below include
cover, contents and editorial material; they are extraction diagnostics, not
numbers of legislative paragraphs. Source cover controls the snapshot date.

GATE 0.5: PASS — at least two distinct, authentic dated full texts extracted.

Substantive change verified in section 2 between 2020-10-14 and 2021-04-01:
- Old definition uses employed adopting mother, adopting father or sole male adopter.
- 2021 definition uses qualifying adopter or surviving parent.
- Evidence: research/ie-v04/adoptive-leave-2020-2021.diff.

Source defect: index rows 2019-10-24 and 2019-11-01 point to identical S3 objects.
Both PDFs have a 24 October 2019 cover and identical SHA-256. Count six distinct
objects from seven catalogue rows; do not manufacture a 1 November reform.

Dates: Updated to is the consolidation cutoff, not publication. These documents
do not supply the publication date of each consolidation. Do not use PDF creation
metadata or index dates as Source-Date. Resolve the actual affecting instrument,
or omit Source-Date and use the norm publication date under SPEC v0.4.

Classification:
- eISB ordinary enacted Acts: as_enacted, with genuine amendment-history metadata.
- Archived Revised Acts PDF snapshots: point_in_time at their verified cutoff.
- Latest-only Revised Acts HTML endpoint: current unless paired with immutable
  dated source evidence for the exact text; never apply it to every historic date.
- Constitution current HTML: current until authentic historical texts are sourced.

The Digital Services Act 2024 comparison additionally demonstrates that different
dated PDFs may differ only in editorial cover text. Dates alone do not prove a
new legislative body. Avoid synthetic reform commits for editorial differences.

GATE 0.7: source inventory and required scope established; support for historical
PDF must be implemented and cross-format fidelity validated before production.
Redistribution permission for LRC material remains a production gate.
